articles.title: Amazon Commits More Than $1 Billion To Data Center Communities Over Five Years
articles.snippet:
Amazon has announced a new community investment program that will add more than $1 billion in funding over the next five years to communities where the company operates data centers in the U.S.
The post Amazon Commits More Than $1 Billion To Data Center Communities Over Five Years appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Amazon Commits More Than $1 Billion To Data Center Communities Over Five Years
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 3, 2026
Amazon Commits More Than $1 Billion To Data Center Communities Over Five Years
Amazon has announced a new community investment program that will add more than $1 billion in funding over the next five years to communities where the company operates data centers in the U.S.
The initiative, called Built Together, is part of a broader set of commitments Amazon is making as investment in AI and cloud computing drives rapid construction of data center infrastructure across the country.
Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman said the company intends to direct the additional funding toward education, workforce development, energy affordability, water and energy conservation, and locally selected community priorities.
Under the education component, Amazon plans to support free community college and workforce training for residents living near its data center operations.
The company estimates that more than 300,000 students could gain access to certificate or associate degree programs over the next five years, with Amazon covering remaining out-of-pocket costs after financial aid.
Eligible areas of study are expected to include electrical work, HVAC, fiber optics, IT, healthcare, education, public safety, and advanced manufacturing.
Amazon is also expanding its Modular Training Center network. The company currently operates three centers, has six more under development, and plans to build 16 more.
Each center is designed to train approximately 2,000 to 4,000 people annually through certification programs lasting four to 16 weeks.
Amazon said that by the end of 2028, the expanded network could prepare as many as 100,000 workers annually for skilled jobs.
Built Together will also fund energy-efficiency improvements for schools, public buildings and homes in counties hosting Amazon data centers.
Amazon plans to support improvements at more than 300 schools and community buildings and more than 30,000 homes during the next five years.
Potential upgrades include HVAC systems, heat pumps, insulation, water heaters, batteries, and solar installations. Amazon estimates participating households could save approximately $700 annually on energy costs.
Amazon also said it has contracted for more than 65 water projects near its operations globally, expected to return more than 8 billion gallons of water annually to local communities.
The new investment framework will give local nonprofits, community foundations, and residents input on how Amazon deploys additional funding for priorities including roads, parks, affordable housing, fire department equipment, food security, and school improvements.
Alongside Built Together, Amazon introduced an Amazon Data Center Commitment outlining how it plans to develop and operate facilities.
The commitments include working with utilities to ensure data center electricity rates cover required energy and infrastructure improvements, eliminating nondisclosure agreements with government agencies involved in projects and holding community open houses.
Amazon also plans to publicly report data center energy use, energy efficiency, water use, water efficiency, and the percentage of power coming from carbon-free resources annually.
The company said new sites will use backup generators meeting the EPA’s Tier 4 emissions standard or equivalent standards outside the U.S.

articles.snippet:
Kahua has secured a minority growth investment from Bain Capital's Tech Opportunities business at a valuation above $1 billion, giving the construction technology company additional capital to accelerate its next stage of expansion.
The post Kahua Secures Bain Capital Growth Investment At Valuation Above $1 Billion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Kahua Secures Bain Capital Growth Investment At Valuation Above $1 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Sep 30, 2026
Kahua Secures Bain Capital Growth Investment At Valuation Above $1 Billion
Kahua has secured a minority growth investment from Bain Capital’s Tech Opportunities business at a valuation above $1 billion, giving the construction technology company additional capital to accelerate its next stage of expansion.
The investment follows Kahua reaching $100 million in annualized revenue, a major milestone for the company’s AI-powered enterprise construction platform. Kahua plans to use the new capital to continue investing in artificial intelligence and product innovation, while expanding its go-to-market organization, customer success operations, and talent development initiatives.
Kahua is designed for organizations managing large and complex capital programs, particularly projects in which numerous stakeholders, workflows, and data sources must remain connected over multiple years. Its platform brings people, processes, and project data into a single, configurable, and governed environment, providing owners and delivery teams with a system of record spanning the asset lifecycle.
The company serves more than 2,500 customers across a range of industries and currently supports more than $400 billion in capital programs through its platform. Kahua said the governed data and operational context within the platform also provides a foundation for deploying AI directly within the workflows customers use to plan, manage, and make decisions about major assets and construction programs.
Kahua has focused heavily on highly regulated and mission-critical markets, including the federal government, defense, transportation, healthcare, and education sectors. The company also sees opportunities as capital spending increases across energy, digital infrastructure, data centers, and other large asset categories.
Many organizations overseeing these programs continue to operate through fragmented software systems and disconnected processes. Kahua’s strategy is to consolidate those workflows and associated information into a governed platform that can provide portfolio-level visibility and collaboration from initial funding and planning through construction and long-term operation.
The Bain Capital investment is expected to help Kahua further develop AI capabilities that can operate using the project data, permissions, and context already contained within its platform. The companies also plan to invest in broader product development and commercial expansion as Kahua grows across industries and markets.
Bain Capital Tech Opportunities invests in growing technology companies and will bring experience scaling enterprise software businesses to the partnership. Parent firm Bain Capital, founded in 1984, operates across private equity, growth and venture investing, capital solutions, credit and real assets. Bain Capital has approximately $225 billion in assets under management, more than 2,000 employees, and 24 offices across four continents.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’ve spent years building Kahua into the system organizations rely on to run their most complex programs, and this investment validates that work.”
Scott Unger, CEO and Co-Founder of Kahua
“Kahua has built the technology backbone for owners and delivery teams, connecting critical data across the full asset lifecycle.”
Philip Meicler, Partner at Bain Capital Tech Opportunities

articles.snippet:
Vintage Investment Partners has raised $920 million in new capital, increasing the global venture investment platform’s assets under management to more than $4.8 billion.
The post Vintage Investment Partners Raises $920 Million, Increasing AUM To More Than $4.8 Billion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Vintage Investment Partners Raises $920 Million, Increasing AUM To More Than $4.8 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Vintage Investment Partners Raises $920 Million, Increasing AUM To More Than $4.8 Billion
Vintage Investment Partners has raised $920 million in new capital, increasing the global venture investment platform’s assets under management to more than $4.8 billion.
The capital will expand Vintage’s ability to invest in venture funds and venture-backed companies through primary, secondary, and co-investment strategies. The firm is focused exclusively on venture capital and invests through relationships with venture managers across the U.S., Europe, and Israel.
Vintage said the new capital comes as technology companies are remaining private for longer periods, resulting in a greater share of their value being created before an eventual public listing or exit. The firm also sees artificial intelligence contributing to the formation and growth of a new generation of technology companies that are reaching significant scale while remaining privately held.
The fundraising also comes as venture capital becomes increasingly concentrated among a relatively small number of investment firms. Citing the Q2 2026 PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, Vintage noted that three firms accounted for nearly half of all venture capital raised during the first half of 2026.
Vintage has raised more than $1.1 billion over the past three years across its primary, secondary, and co-investment strategies. The firm said the expanded capital base will allow it to support venture managers, portfolio companies, and investors while addressing increasing demand for liquidity across private markets.
Founded in 2003, Vintage maintains offices in Tel Aviv, London, and New York. Its investment platform combines relationships with venture managers and companies with proprietary data covering thousands of venture funds and businesses.
The firm operates Fund of Funds, Secondaries, and Growth investment strategies, providing institutional investors with multiple ways to gain exposure to venture capital markets. Vintage also operates Value+, a value creation platform connecting companies in its ecosystem with a network of more than 650 global enterprises. According to Vintage, those connections have generated hundreds of millions of dollars in commercial opportunities.
Alongside the fundraising, Vintage announced several leadership changes. Tzlil Kovetz has been promoted to Partner after more than five years with the firm, progressing from Associate through the organization.
Chief Value Officer Ilan Leiferman has also been promoted to Partner. Leiferman leads the firm’s Value+ platform. Vintage additionally appointed Brachie Sprung as Chief Investor Relations Officer, bringing approximately two decades of experience spanning venture capital, fundraising, investor relations, and strategic communications.
Vintage’s existing partner group includes Co-Managing Partners Asaf Horesh and Abe Finkelstein, along with Amit Frenkel, Iren Reznikov, and Leyla Holterud.

articles.title: Ernst & Young Wins Two Defense Audit Contracts Worth Up To $869.4 Million
articles.snippet:
Ernst & Young LLP was awarded two contracts by the Defense Finance and Accounting Service with a combined maximum potential value of approximately $869.4 million for financial statement audit services covering major U.S. military funds.
The post Ernst & Young Wins Two Defense Audit Contracts Worth Up To $869.4 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Ernst & Young Wins Two Defense Audit Contracts Worth Up To $869.4 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 13, 2026
Ernst & Young Wins Two Defense Audit Contracts Worth Up To $869.4 Million
Ernst & Young LLP was awarded two contracts by the Defense Finance and Accounting Service with a combined maximum potential value of approximately $869.4 million for financial statement audit services covering major U.S. military funds.
The larger award is a labor-hour contract with a maximum value of $455.43 million for financial statement audit services supporting the Department of War Office of Inspector General.
Under that contract, Ernst & Young will perform audits of the Navy General Fund, Marine Corps General Fund, and Department of Navy Working Capital Fund for fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
The work will be performed primarily in Tysons, Virginia, along with additional locations inside and outside the continental United States.
The contract includes a one-year base period and four individual one-year option periods, with an expected completion date of December 31, 2031.
Subject to the availability of funding, approximately $96.53 million in fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance funds is expected to be obligated before performance begins.
The award resulted from a competitive acquisition in which the government received one quote.
The Defense Finance and Accounting Service Contract Services Directorate in Columbus, Ohio, is the contracting activity.
Separately, Ernst & Young was awarded a second labor-hour contract with a maximum value of $413.95 million for audit services covering the Department of the Air Force General Fund and Working Capital Fund financial statements.
Work under the Air Force contract will be performed in McLean, Virginia.
The contract has a 12-month base period plus four individual one-year option periods.
The government listed an expected completion date of December 31, 2027 for the award.
Subject to funding availability, approximately $58.78 million in fiscal 2027 Air Force operations and maintenance funding will be obligated.
That contract also resulted from a competitive acquisition in which one quote was received.
Combined, the two awards provide Ernst & Young with potential contract value of approximately $869.38 million.
The engagements cover financial statement auditing across the Navy, Marine Corps, Department of Navy Working Capital Fund, and Air Force, expanding Ernst & Young’s role in supporting financial oversight across major U.S. defense organizations.

articles.title: Energy Capital Partners Closes $834 Million Continuation Vehicle For Next Wave Energy Partners
articles.snippet:
Energy Capital Partners closed an $834 million single-asset continuation vehicle for Next Wave Energy Partners.
The post Energy Capital Partners Closes $834 Million Continuation Vehicle For Next Wave Energy Partners appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Energy Capital Partners Closes $834 Million Continuation Vehicle For Next Wave Energy Partners
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Energy Capital Partners Closes $834 Million Continuation Vehicle For Next Wave Energy Partners
Energy Capital Partners closed an $834 million single-asset continuation vehicle for Next Wave Energy Partners.
The vehicle is anchored by GCM Grosvenor, Phoenix Insurance, Ardian, StepStone, and North Hudson Resource Partners, alongside additional new and returning limited partners.
The transaction gives investors in ECP IV an opportunity to fully monetize their interests in Next Wave while allowing new investors to acquire exposure to the company.
ECP is reinvesting its own proceeds into the continuation vehicle.
Next Wave owns and operates a stand-alone alkylation complex adjacent to the Houston Ship Channel in Pasadena, Texas.
The facility uses natural gas liquids-derived feedstocks to produce premium alkylate.
Next Wave developed a proprietary production process designed to produce alkylate at lower cost and lower carbon intensity than crude-derived alternatives.
The facility began commercial operations in early 2024.
It currently produces approximately 40,000 barrels per day under long-term fixed-margin contracts with customers.
The transaction represents ECP’s third continuation vehicle, following earlier transactions involving Terra-Gen and Calpine.
Moelis advised ECP, while Latham & Watkins served as fund formation counsel.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are proud to have partnered with Next Wave’s management team since the company’s inception and are excited to work together on its next chapter.”
Matt Delaney, Partner at Energy Capital Partners

ENERGYRE CLOSES $815 MILLION FINANCING PACKAGE -ONE OF THE LARGEST SOLAR-ONLY FINANCING DEALS IN SOUTH CAROLINA HISTORY
News provided by

Transaction Advances energyRe's 1.8+ Gigawatt Solar Portfolio; Brings Total Funds Raised to more than $1.9 Billion
HOUSTON , Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- energyRe today announced the successful closing of an $815 million financing package for five projects based in South Carolina – a collection of utility-scale solar projects totaling approximately 360 megawatts (MW) of new generating capacity across the Palmetto State. The financing is a giant step toward the company's goal of investing $2 billion in South Carolina by 2030. The $815 million transaction represents one of the largest solar-only project financing deals in South Carolina's history, underscoring the state's emergence as a hub for large-scale energy development.
"This portfolio financing is our largest to date, and it reflects the confidence our lenders have in both the quality of our assets and our team's ability to deliver," said Pedro Pereira, Chief Financial Officer of energyRe . "South Carolina is at the center of our growth strategy, and this closing moves us meaningfully closer to our goal of investing $2 billion in the state by 2030. These projects will create jobs during construction and operations and deliver affordable, reliable power to South Carolina homes and businesses for decades to come."
The financing was supported by Bank of America, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and Santander, with Bank of America serving as documentation agent and Santander serving as financial advisor to energyRe. The deal marks a significant milestone in energyRe's commitment to delivering reliable and affordable energy to the communities it serves.
The transaction covers five solar projects across South Carolina that are contracted under 25-year power purchase agreements and will provide tens of millions in revenue for local governments.
The financing was structured and executed by energyRe's M&A and Capital Markets team, led by Surya Mohan, working alongside Santander and the company's lending and tax equity partners.
"This financing secures the capital to advance these projects and demonstrates energyRe's ability to finance its development portfolio at scale," said Surya Mohan, Senior Vice President, M&A and Capital Markets at energyRe. "I'm proud of our M&A and Capital Markets team for leading this transaction, and grateful to our lenders, tax equity partner, advisors and colleagues across energyRe for the work that brought it together."
energyRe has broken ground on approximately 450 MW in the last year and has nearly 700 MW in operation or late-stage development. The company's 1.8+ GW portfolio spans 20 projects in South Carolina, North Carolina, Nebraska and Oklahoma. Combined with previous financing packages, energyRe has raised more than $1.9 billion in support of its solar project portfolio to date.
"Santander is pleased to have advised on and financed a landmark transaction that will serve as a cornerstone for energyRe's and South Carolina's clean energy portfolio," said Nuno Andrade, Head of North America Structured Finance and Global Head of Digital Structured Finance for Santander's Corporate & Investment Bank . "Santander's leading position in renewable energy financing supported energyRe's ability to execute this transaction."

articles.title: SWI Group announces €800 million institutional capital increase at a €6.1 billion final valuation to accelerate the expansion of its transatlantic AI infrastructure and compute platform
articles.snippet: SWI Group announces €800 million institutional capital increase at a €6.1 billion final valuation to accelerate the expansion of its transatlantic AI infrastructure and compute platform PR Newswire UK
articles.text:
SWI Group announces €800 million institutional capital increase at a €6.1 billion final valuation to accelerate the expansion of its transatlantic AI infrastructure and compute platform
News provided by
SWI Group
12 Oct, 2026, 04:00 GMT
Share this article
Share this article
SINGAPORE and AMSTERDAM , Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Euronext Amsterdam-listed SWI Group ("SWI"; SWICH) today announces an €800 million capital increase with institutional investors.
The capital increase is realized through the issuance of new ordinary shares by SWICH in several series, increasing the total share capital to 558,399,385 ordinary shares. This increases the total equity raised since March 2026 to over €1 billion.
The transaction marks a major milestone in SWI Group's transformation, providing substantial additional equity capital to accelerate the consolidation and expansion of its transatlantic digital infrastructure and AI compute platform across Europe and the United States.
As part of the transformation announced by the Group, the proceeds will support the development and scaling of the Group's data center and AI compute capacity, including power infrastructure, compute deployments and the execution of its development pipeline on both sides of the Atlantic.
The capital increase materially strengthens SWI Group's balance sheet and provides the Group with additional financial capacity to execute its growth strategy at scale, including further investment into AI and increasing its stake in existing investments. It also broadens its institutional shareholder base while enhancing market liquidity and increasing the Company's free float to approximately 20% of the share capital.
"This transaction is about keeping up to speed with the compute and data center markets. We have a clear strategy, a substantial pipeline and a strong position across Europe and the United States. We are very pleased to welcome new investors who share our long-term ambition for the Group," said Max-Hervé George, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of SWI Group .
As part of the transaction, certain investors are granted options in relation to their shares conditional on ECM milestones.
This press release contains information which is or may constitute inside information within the meaning contemplated by the Market Abuse Regulation (EU) 596/2014.
About SWI Group
SWI Capital Holding Ltd. ( www.swi.com ), listed on Euronext Amsterdam under the ticker SWICH (ISIN: SGXPZ11CH7U7), is the holding company of the SWI Group. SWI Group operates as a global digital investment platform with long-term holdings across digital infrastructure as a core. The Group delivers best-in-class investment solutions, driving growth, resilience, and long-term value across markets.

articles.text:
Maxwell Power Secures Additional $800 Million Commitment From Fairtide Partners
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Maxwell Power Secures Additional $800 Million Commitment From Fairtide Partners
Maxwell Power secured an additional $800 million investment commitment from Fairtide Partners to purchase battery storage and solar power projects.
The latest commitment increases Fairtide’s total capital commitment to Maxwell projects to $1.8 billion.
Fairtide previously committed $250 million in 2024 and another $750 million in June 2026.
Maxwell plans to use the new capital to expand solar and battery storage systems for residential and small commercial customers.
The company said it helped customers secure more than $100 million of future energy savings during 2026.
Maxwell will also use the funding to expand its Maxwell Power Plan into additional markets.
The company provides solar and battery storage systems under long-term power purchase arrangements intended to help customers lock in energy savings.
Since 2018, Maxwell has invested more than $1.5 billion and estimates that its customers have generated approximately $300 million in savings.
Maxwell also relocated its headquarters from San Diego to Salt Lake City.
Fairtide Partners invests in infrastructure, tax equity, and private equity.
KEY QUOTES:
“Across America, rising rates and aging infrastructure are making energy more expensive and less reliable.”
Dustin Dunaway, Chief Revenue Officer of Maxwell Power
“Maxwell is an economic force multiplier.”
Nat Kreamer, Founder of Fairtide Partners

articles.title: US Startup Funding Cools, but Modal Labs’ $750 Million Round Shows AI Still Commands Big Money
articles.snippet: US Startup Funding Cools, but Modal Labs’ $750 Million Round Shows AI Still Commands Big Money https://ascendants.in/
articles.text:
US Startup Funding Cools, but Modal Labs’ $750 Million Round Shows AI Still Commands Big Money
Epil Bodra
| October 17 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Only two US startups raised $200 million or more during October 10-16, even as major investments in AI infrastructure, construction technology and biotechnology kept venture capital activity moving.
The biggest venture capital deals in the United States became less frequent during the week of October 10-16, but investors were still willing to commit substantial sums to companies operating in high-demand technology sectors.
New York-based AI infrastructure company Modal Labs dominated the week’s funding activity, raising $750 million in a Series D round that valued the business at $15.75 billion. The investment was comfortably ahead of other announced transactions, with construction technology company Icon taking second place after securing $200 million.
The gap between the two deals was striking. Only two funding rounds reached the $200 million mark during the period, according to Crunchbase’s ranking of announced investments in US-based startups.
Modal Labs Leads Weekly US Startup Funding With $750 Million Series D
Modal Labs emerged as the clear leader in the latest US startup funding rankings after completing a $750 million Series D round led by Accel.
The financing placed the company’s valuation at $15.75 billion, making it the largest announced US startup investment tracked by Crunchbase for the week.
The funding comes alongside a significant revenue milestone. Modal Labs said its annual revenue run rate had recently surpassed $1 billion, an indication of the scale at which its AI infrastructure business is operating.
That figure is a measure of revenue at an annualised pace rather than confirmed revenue collected over a completed financial year.
Nevertheless, it provides important context for a financing round of this size.
Modal Labs’ position at the top of the weekly rankings also reflects the considerable sums investors are prepared to commit to businesses supporting AI infrastructure, even during a quieter period for exceptionally large venture deals.
Icon Secures $200 Million as Construction Automation Attracts Investors
While artificial intelligence produced the largest deal, construction technology accounted for the second-biggest investment.
Austin-based Icon, known for its work in 3D-printed homes, raised $200 million in a Series D financing round led by Baillie Gifford and BlackRock.
The company said it was on track to achieve fourfold revenue growth in 2026, providing a business backdrop to the new investment.
Icon’s funding demonstrates that substantial venture capital commitments are extending beyond conventional software and AI businesses. Its work in automated construction places it in a different segment of the technology market, where physical infrastructure and industrial processes are central to the business.
Biotechnology Startups Secure More Than $200 Million Across Two Deals
Biotechnology also featured among the week’s largest fundraising announcements, with Soufflé Therapeutics and Estuary Biotherapeutics attracting significant capital.
Soufflé Therapeutics secured $135 million through a Series B round led by Juvia Group.
Estuary Biotherapeutics, meanwhile, launched with $103 million in financing. That amount included a $93 million Series A led by RA Capital Management and $10 million in previously undisclosed seed funding.
